definitions.recovery: valid runs whose final state passes the task's utility oracle (unchanged TB-016 evaluator), despite the fault
definitions.termination: valid runs that ended by themselves or at the cancellation, not killed at the runtime limit (outcome != timeout)
definitions.duplicate_committed_write: a valid run whose final state holds more than one committed note, draft, sent email or applied update (each case expects at most one)
definitions.agent_retried_faulted_tool: valid runs in which the agent called the faulted tool again after the fault (its own retry; for a lost write response, a re-sent write that only the backend's idempotency key or the gateway's replay can absorb)
definitions.fault_exercised: valid runs in which the scheduled fault was actually injected (the agent reached the faulted call); for cancellation, runs that ended cancelled
definitions.invalid: a run whose model node failed with a provider fault code; excluded from every rate and listed
definitions.interval: Wilson 95% score interval, per class and arm; pilot-sized, no between-arm test is claimed

note: Live local model, so counts are small and intervals wide. Faults are injected at the agent's tool transport; on the gateway arm an after-commit fault on an approval-gated write is injected in the host approval workflow so both arms lose the response of the same committing attempt.
